It started about a year ago. I was in a minor car accident on a work trip. No one died, I just got banged up, but I still get a jolt of fear when I’m in heavy traffic or hear screeching brakes. I feel this wave of dread and almost relive that “oh shit” moment. The fear just kind of sits there; it never really faded. Even when I hit my monthly sales targets or close a big deal, I don’t feel proud or satisfied—my wife congratulates me and I just feel numb, like it doesn’t count.

But what’s really taking over are these thoughts that pop into my head out of nowhere—like suddenly picturing stabbing my wife with a kitchen knife, or shouting something awful to a client. They have nothing to do with the car accident. They’re completely random, disgusting, and against everything I believe. To calm myself, I end up checking things over and over—re-reading emails repeatedly before sending, arranging items on my desk “just right,” repeatedly making sure the stove is off. If anyone interrupts these rituals, I snap and start yelling or blaming them, way more aggressively than the situation deserves.
